summary: The last 4 weeks show a severely fragmented training block: only 9 sessions completed, dominated by open-water swims and sporadic runs, with a single long ride on July 20. Recovery metrics are critically concerning — multiple nights of under 3 hours of sleep, body battery readings regularly below 30, and a near-complete collapse in the final week of July (41 min sleep on July 27, body battery of 2 on July 30) indicate accumulated fatigue that makes meaningful training adaptation impossible right now. With the Half Oceanman 63 days away requiring a 5km open-water swim at 2:30/100m, and the Treviso 10K 71 days away at 5:45/km, the immediate priority is rebuilding sleep and recovery before resuming structured load.
suggestions: Sleep is the single highest-leverage intervention right now — target 7+ hours nightly for the next 10 days before resuming any session with a training load above 60; use body battery ≥50 on waking as a daily green light to train.

Swim volume must become your training priority given the Half Oceanman (5km OW) in 63 days: aim for 3 pool sessions per week from Week 7 onward, progressively building from 1,500m to 3,000m+ per session, with at least one open-water session per week in Malta's warm sea.

The July 18 run at 179 bpm average HR (training load 208) against a backdrop of poor sleep almost certainly contributed to the crash that followed — reintroduce running conservatively at HR ≤140 bpm before adding any pace work.

Add at least one open-water swim to Week 9 (Aug 22 morning) as planned, prioritising race-simulation pacing at 2:25–2:30/100m over the bike distance that week — the swim is the limiter for your nearest A-race.

For the Treviso 10K (71 days), pace-specific work at 5:45/km should only begin once you are sleeping consistently — the Week 9 and Week 10 interval sessions in the plan are appropriately timed but are contingent on the recovery gate being met.

proposed_changes.current_session: Pool swim 45 min, ~1,500m easy aerobic with 400m technique drills + 4×100m at 2:20–2:30/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Pool swim 45 min, 1,200–1,500m total: 300m warm-up, 6×100m at 2:25–2:30/100m with 20-sec rest (race-pace familiarisation), 300m cool-down — skip entirely if waking body battery is below 45.
proposed_changes.reason: Introducing race-pace intervals early (even at low volume) builds 2:30/100m familiarity for the Half Oceanman 63 days away, while the reduced total volume respects the current depleted recovery state.

proposed_changes.current_session: Pool session: min 2,000m, mix of technique drills and aerobic sets at ≤2:30/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Pool session 55–60 min: 2,000m structured — 400m warm-up, 4×400m at 2:25–2:30/100m with 30-sec rest, 400m cool-down; prioritise consistent split holding over speed.
proposed_changes.reason: Progressing the Friday swim to race-specific sets of 400m repeats at target Half Oceanman pace builds the aerobic repeatability needed for a 5km OW race in 9 weeks.

proposed_changes.current_session: Replace long run with 45–50 min OW or pool swim at easy aerobic effort, 1,500–1,800m; skip run unless sleep averaged 6.5h Aug 4–8
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 45–50 min open-water swim at Malta coast, 1,500–1,800m at easy 2:35–2:40/100m — this replaces the long run entirely; use the session to practice sighting, drafting position, and steady pacing rather than hitting a distance target.
proposed_changes.reason: With the Half Oceanman as the nearest A-race and running still constrained by fatigue, substituting a second weekly OW swim accelerates swim-specific adaptation without adding run injury risk.

proposed_changes.current_session: 92km @ 128–177W (Z2 Endurance), option to add 3×10min Z3 Tempo blocks
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 92km @ 128–160W (Z2, lower half only), no tempo blocks — treat as a pure aerobic long ride; do not add Z3 blocks this week regardless of how good you feel, as Wk8 is the first full-load week after a recovery deficit.
proposed_changes.reason: Adding Z3 tempo in the first properly-loaded week after a severe recovery crash risks another fatigue spike; keep Week 8's long ride aerobic to ensure the subsequent run and swim sessions can also be completed.

proposed_changes.current_session: 60 min pool session: 2,500m with Half Oceanman-specific set — 400m warm-up, 3×600m @ 2:25/100m with 30-sec rest, 300m cool-down
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 60 min pool session: 2,500m — 400m warm-up, 3×600m @ 2:22–2:25/100m with 25-sec rest, 400m pull-buoy cool-down at relaxed pace; if splits drift beyond 2:30/100m on rep 2–3, shorten to 2×600m and add an extra 200m drill set.
proposed_changes.reason: Tightening the rest interval to 25 seconds and adding a split-based bail-out rule makes this set a more accurate Half Oceanman race simulation while preventing over-reaching if fitness is still building.

proposed_changes.current_session: 60–75 min Z1–low-Z2 spin at 128–145W after a morning OW swim; reduce ride to 75–80km to manage total daily load
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Morning: 45–60 min OW swim (1,500–2,000m at 2:25–2:30/100m) as planned. Afternoon: reduce ride to 60 min flat Z1 spin at 120–135W maximum — do not target 75–80km distance, just time on the bike; total daily training load should not exceed 180.
proposed_changes.reason: The morning OW swim is the race-priority session that day; capping the afternoon ride power and removing a distance target ensures the swim quality is not compromised by accumulated fatigue within the same day.
